video_title: Head Coach Jordan Ott Postgame Media Availability | 10-30-26

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamal Murray's impact as a high-level shot maker
quotes.excerpt: He's been a big-time shot maker. I've been on the other side of it multiple times.
quotes.quote: Jamal Murray was a big part of that. He started five of five. When we start to close the gap and you can feel the energy rise, he'd make another one. That's what he does. He's been a big-time shot maker. I've been on the other side of it multiple times. No different tonight.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott on Jamal Murray's performance tonight: He's been a big-time shot maker. I've been on the other side of it multiple times. No different tonight.

structured.context: Head coach Jordan Ott discusses the impact of Jamal Murray's shot-making during the postgame media availability.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Defensive intensity and execution struggles against Denver
quotes.excerpt: There's a piece to execution that we need too. There's going to be some of those moments.
quotes.quote: At periods that was us. That was our energy, that was our intensity, and then there's a piece to execution that we need too. There's going to be some of those moments where, give them credit, they've been a top-five offense for the last five, six years. They were number one offense last year, and they got some shot making from a guy that's made five all year, made seven, believe that's his career high, I would guess. We were trying to take it out of Nikola Jokic's hands at times. The ball found him, especially in the first half, Jamal Murray, and he made them.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott on the defensive challenge of facing Denver: We were trying to take it out of Nikola Jokic's hands at times. The ball found him, especially in the first half, Jamal Murray, and he made them.

structured.context: Jordan Ott reflects on the team's defensive intensity and the challenge of defending Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Defensive breakdowns and transition issues against Denver
quotes.excerpt: Sometimes in transition they can't get a wide open layup at the other end.
quotes.quote: Sometimes in transition they can't get a wide open layup at the other end. That's one. There's post defense, of course it changes with Nikola Jokic. We were double teaming him, but it was on the dribble. Sometimes we just go, and then that near shooter, which happened to be Jamal Murray multiple times, and then on top of it, we fouled him. We put them on the line 30 times. A team that doesn't really drive you, drive you like we've seen, and we did handle their off-ball splits to a certain degree.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott on defensive breakdowns: Sometimes we just go, and then that near shooter, which happened to be Jamal Murray multiple times, and then on top of it, we fouled him. We put them on the line 30 times.

structured.context: Jordan Ott explains the defensive breakdowns and transition issues the team faced against Denver.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Need for better ball pressure against Denver's passing
quotes.excerpt: That's where we need better ball pressure on the best passer, passing big in the league.
quotes.quote: There's some where they're just physically bigger than us. Aaron Gordon got there a couple times. They just were able to throw over top. That's where we need better ball pressure on the best passer, passing big in the league, or we need to change. That's some of those things that they put you in. We've seen these guys so many times in the fourth quarter. They're one of the best execution teams in the fourth quarter, and I thought our intensity in that fourth quarter was pretty good to really give us a chance there.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott on defending Nikola Jokic: We need better ball pressure on the best passer, passing big in the league, or we need to change. They are one of the best execution teams in the fourth quarter.

structured.context: Jordan Ott discusses the need for better ball pressure to counter the size and passing ability of Denver's players.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Chet Holmgren's defensive intensity and team resilience
quotes.excerpt: That's the Chet Holmgren intensity. Goodies on-ball defense, that takes some time away.
quotes.quote: I think part of it is the positive of Chet Holmgren. That's the Chet Holmgren intensity. Goodies on-ball defense, that takes some time away. But this is an 82-game season. There's ups and downs to it all. I think what makes us different and our group different, we're sticking through thick and thin. We're going to work right beside you. One night it's this from someone, we'll pick them back up. Tonight, Jalen didn't have it. He didn't have it all there, and we'll be right beside him to pick him back up. We need everyone.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott on team culture: This is an 82-game season. There's ups and downs to it all. I think what makes us different and our group different, we're sticking through thick and thin.

structured.context: Jordan Ott praises Chet Holmgren's intensity and discusses the team's need to support Jalen Williams after a tough performance.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Nikola Jokic's craftiness and ability to manipulate rotations
quotes.excerpt: He's so crafty. Not all the time does he hit the next rotation. He loves to skip.
quotes.quote: The tough part about Nikola Jokic is he's so crafty. Not all the time does he hit the next rotation. He loves to skip the rotation. You're worried about the cutters, but we were going on the bounce, and then you feel the pressure at times to go before he dribbles. So he's just sitting there surveying. That's the ones that got us early, or through three quarters. And then, just him in general, he just puts you in so many different situations. Then they play pick and roll and they hit him at 10 feet, and that's hard to stop.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott on the difficulty of guarding Nikola Jokic: The tough part about Nikola Jokic is he's so crafty. Not all the time does he hit the next rotation. He loves to skip the rotation.

structured.context: Jordan Ott describes the difficulty of defending Nikola Jokic due to his craftiness and ability to manipulate defensive rotations.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Miles Bridges' offensive versatility and defensive growth
quotes.excerpt: We're learning, right? You can see all of it, the three-point shooting, where he's going to find his spots.
quotes.quote: We're learning, right? You can see all of it, the three-point shooting, where he's going to find his spots, but also his ability to get to the rim. He can finish with both hands. Love him in transition. We're learning, can he initiate some offense? Can he be a roller in some of those situations? He's obviously with our small ball lineup right now, too. And then with Dylan Windler out, we put a lot of stress on him there in that second half. But you can feel his defensive intensity. We've been on him about not just staying in front of the opponent, physically getting up and into the ball handler, and that's a test. Aaron Gordon's a really good player, and I thought he did that and you could feel the whole building rise with his defensive intensity.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott on Miles Bridges: You can feel his defensive intensity. We've been on him about not just staying in front of the opponent, physically getting up and into the ball handler, and that's a test.

structured.context: Jordan Ott evaluates Miles Bridges' versatility and defensive intensity while noting Dylan Windler's absence.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Addressing free throw disparity and late-game execution
quotes.excerpt: We see the same free throw disparity you do. Nikola Jokic takes over the game.
quotes.quote: We see the same free throw disparity you do. So again, I thought we got to a spot there midway through the fourth, and Nikola Jokic takes over the game by the ability to draw a whistle. That's playing simply what he does. He just changes the dynamic in so many different ways. He felt it just like we all felt it that we were coming. Six-point game, eight-point game and the 50-50 call when we lay the ball in. That's some of the things that he does at a high level.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott on the free throw disparity against Denver: Nikola Jokic takes over the game by the ability to draw a whistle. That's playing simply what he does. He just changes the dynamic in so many different ways.

structured.context: Jordan Ott comments on the free throw disparity and Nikola Jokic's ability to influence the game through officiating.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Offensive ball movement and team performance against Oklahoma City
quotes.excerpt: I thought at times in Golden State definitely did, and then they zoned us.
quotes.quote: I thought at times in Golden State definitely did, and then they zoned us. They zoned us 33 possessions in Oklahoma City, and Oklahoma City is a team that if you make the next pass, you just run the risk of turning the ball over. So I thought in Oklahoma City we took care of the ball. I think we had 12 turnovers, and got really high quality shots. Again, 39 catch and shoot threes. Now it was a different defense tonight. This team, we can put these teams like this in a ton of close outs because of how much they shrink the floor, and I thought at times our ball movement was probably the best of the year.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott on the team's offensive progress: This team, we can put these teams like this in a ton of close outs because of how much they shrink the floor, and I thought at times our ball movement was probably the best of the year.

structured.context: Jordan Ott analyzes the team's offensive ball movement and performance in recent games against Golden State and Oklahoma City.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Communication and scheme adjustments regarding Nikola Jokic
quotes.excerpt: When are we going? It's pretty clear in a practice environment.
quotes.quote: When are we going? It's pretty clear in a practice environment, but then you get nervous at times to let your teammate down there on that island, and if he's not dribbling, his ability just to get it out of his hands, that next guy has to be there on the catch, especially the way he's been shooting it this year. And we, I think it was 55% coming into the night, catch and shoot. So we definitely didn't want that. That one pass away is something we'll clean up.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott on defensive communication: When are we going? It's pretty clear in a practice environment, but then you get nervous at times to let your teammate down there on that island.

structured.context: Jordan Ott discusses the need for better communication and defensive schemes when guarding Nikola Jokic.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Addressing the Dylan Windler foul and officiating
quotes.excerpt: I'm not sure the replay tug as much. I saw it live.
quotes.quote: I'm not sure the replay tug as much. I saw it live. I know players' feet swing all the time. There was a couple possessions before that, I was trying to tell the officials, they are national team teammates. Like they were going back and forth, this is nothing malicious. These guys played together and probably played together forever. So we'll see if we can find another flagrant two on that play around the league. I hope reputation doesn't play into that, but they were just competitive guys going at it like they probably have for 10 years. Just unfortunate that we get the short end of the stick on some of that.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott on the flagrant call involving Dylan Windler: I hope reputation doesn't play into that, but they were just competitive guys going at it like they probably have for 10 years. Just unfortunate that we get the short end of the stick.

structured.context: Jordan Ott reacts to a flagrant foul call involving Dylan Windler and expresses frustration with the officiating.
